summary: @servicetitan/microfront-auth preinstall drops Bun runtime to execute obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares preinstall="node setup.mjs", which runs automatically on npm install. setup.mjs (minified with _0xXXXX identifiers) probes for Bun; if absent, it downloads Bun v1.3.13 from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases, extracts it to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it via execFileSync against the tarball-shipped math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727KB heavily obfuscated @bun-cjs file using a rotating numeric string-array decoder (WV8StW/hc1jfK9) and mangled identifiers, so its runtime behavior, network destinations, and string constants are hidden from static review. The package is published under the @servicetitan scope, ships an empty description, and points repository at github.com/servicetitan/playground.git — a scope-hijack / dependency-confusion framing that lends visual authority to the install-time dropper. An auth microfrontend library has no legitimate need for an alternate runtime or an obfuscated payload; the alternate-runtime dropper pattern is used specifically to hide the executed code from Node-focused scanners.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
